candidates.theme_relation: Core distribution layer for restaurants; benefits if order density, subscription retention, advertising, and logistics efficiency improve faster than courier, regulation, and merchant-fee pressure.

candidates.theme_relation: Restaurant delivery exposure is embedded in a broader two-sided logistics network; the underappreciated angle is cross-platform frequency and membership-driven order density rather than standalone food-delivery app usage.

evidence.claim: DoorDash reported 2025 Total Orders of 3.172B, Marketplace GOV of $102.018B, revenue of $13.717B, and contribution profit of $4.840B; Total Orders grew 23% and Marketplace GOV grew 27% year over year.
DoorDash said it exited 2025 with over 56M MAUs and over 35M combined DashPass, Wolt+, and Deliveroo Plus members.
evidence.source_title: DoorDash Q4 2025 Financial Results Press Release

evidence.claim: Uber reported 2025 Delivery Gross Bookings growth of 22% year over year on a constant-currency basis, primarily driven by increased Delivery Trip volumes; Q4 2025 MAPCs were 202M, up 18% from Q4 2024.

Toast’s 2025 annual report describes its platform as serving restaurant workflows across dine-in, takeout, delivery, catering, and retail, and describes commission-free first-party online ordering intended to reduce reliance on third parties for online orders.

Maplebear/Instacart says it partners with retailers through Instacart Marketplace and retailer-owned online storefronts powered by Instacart Enterprise Platform, including e-commerce, fulfillment, connected stores, ads, marketing, and insights.

Karat Packaging describes itself as a manufacturer and distributor of single-use disposable products used in restaurant and foodservice settings; in 2025, net sales grew 10.7%, volume grew 11.2%, sales to chains and distributors grew 12.5%, and online-channel sales grew 7.4%.

Olo was acquired by Thoma Bravo in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $2.0B; its common stock ceased trading and was to be delisted from NYSE, so it is not a current US-listed candidate despite high node relevance.
evidence.source_title: Thoma Bravo Completes Acquisition of Olo

evidence.claim: Pactiv Evergreen, another highly relevant foodservice-packaging asset, was acquired by Novolex and is no longer an independent public candidate.
evidence.source_title: Novolex and Pactiv Evergreen Complete Combination

memory_update.text: DASH and UBER remain the cleanest US-listed direct expressions of profitable delivery-density economics, but their chokepoint quality should be measured by contribution/adjusted EBITDA per order, membership retention, and regulatory sensitivity rather than app downloads.

TOST is a second-order supplier to off-premises ordering because first-party digital ordering, POS, payments, loyalty, and operational integrations can help restaurants capture off-premises demand with less marketplace dependence.
KRT is a below-USD-1B exception because it is directly tied to takeout/delivery packaging intensity and may be more chokepoint-relevant than larger but more diversified paper/packaging companies.

CART should be tracked as an adjacent density platform rather than a restaurant pure play; its relevance depends on whether grocery/convenience/prepared-food delivery shares fulfillment infrastructure, ad budgets, and consumer subscriptions with restaurant delivery.

OLO and PTVE were highly relevant public-market mappings for first-party restaurant ordering and foodservice packaging, respectively, but both are no longer current US-listed equities after 2025 take-private/acquisition transactions.

node: Off-premises ordering, delivery marketplaces, pickup, and last-mile density
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the off-premises/delivery-density node. The strongest direct exposures are delivery networks with scale and subscription density, while underappreciated second-order exposures include restaurant operating systems, grocery/retail last-mile platforms with fulfillment-density overlap, and disposable foodservice packaging suppliers tied to takeout and delivery volume. Olo would have been a highly relevant first-party ordering candidate, but it was acquired by Thoma Bravo and delisted in September 2025, so it is treated as a coverage gap rather than a current US-listed candidate.
